title: 1.4.0 is out: Treasure Foxes are here
author: AdWilling6074

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/AdWilling6074 please add some details about how you used AI to develop this. Saying you used AI isn't enough on its own. We're looking for the actual dev details. Rule 4 asks promotional posts to contribute by talking about the process and the actual development. We're trying to keep the sub from filling up with low quality game posts. If this doesn't get updated, it may be removed.

comments.author: AdWilling6074
comments.body:
I'm a solo dev with a full time job, so I've built Grimbit with Claude as basically my coding partner. The art isn't AI, it's the DARK series pixel art packs by Penusbmic which I bought on itch. The music and sound are bought packs too.

The game is in Godot 4.7 with GDScript. My workflow is I decide what goes in and how it should feel, then Claude writes the code straight into my project files on my PC, then I run it on my phone and report back what's broken or feels off. Most features take a few rounds of that. It can't run Godot itself, so all the testing is on me.

Early on we set it up so nearly all the numbers live in one balance json file (enemy stats, drop rates, costs, fox tiers etc), which makes tuning really quick: I can say "bosses feel too tanky in area 4" and it's a data change, not a code change. There's also a little test runner, tests/test_*.gd, that checks things like save files, rewards and the redeem codes, which caught a fair few bugs before players did.

Some concrete examples:

• Treasure foxes use one fox sprite and a shader that maps brightness onto a colour ramp per tier, and the rainbow one cycles hue over time. That saved drawing 5 sprites.
• Skill icons were drawn in code to match each ability.
• When Play Console showed a 13% crash rate, I had it read the stack traces. It was a Godot engine crash on the Vulkan render thread, so we switched mobile to the Compatibility renderer.
• Trailers are recorded with a script that plays a scripted run through Godot's Movie Maker so I get clean footage.
